title: OpenAI previews "Ultrafast" mode, Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash, Claude details watermarks
excerpt: OpenAI previewed a much faster GPT-5.6 Sol, Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash before its delayed Pro model, and Anthropic explained how Claude watermarks will work.

items.h: OpenAI previews Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.t: OpenAI previewed "Ultrafast" mode, which it says runs GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 14 times the speed. It also announced that premium seats are coming to ChatGPT Business.
Reuters reported that Google unveiled Gemini 3.7 Flash, a model for coding and agent workflows. Axios noted it arrives before the long-delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro.

items.h: Anthropic explains how Claude's new watermarks will work
items.t: TechCrunch reported that Anthropic shared more details on how watermarks will work for content made with Claude. Watermarks are hidden signals that help show a piece of content was made by AI.

items.h: Google turns on Gemini for students in Google Classroom
items.t: The New York Times reported that Google turned on Gemini for students using its Classroom app.

water.h: Anthropic on how multi-agent systems go wrong
water.t: Anthropic published research called "Patterns and problems in multiagent systems", on what happens when several AI agents work together. Handy background if you are about to try tools that run many agents at once.

means.t: Watermarks and labels are coming. Be open about AI use in client work and keep a simple log of what AI did and what you did.
If your school switches AI on for students, ask for the written rules first. What counts as help and what counts as cheating should be clear before you use it.
Faster models change what is practical: live meeting notes, instant drafts, quick checks. Pick one slow weekly task and test whether a faster model makes it worth automating.

prompt: Create a one-page "AI use log" template I can fill in for client or work tasks: date, task, tool used, what the AI did, what I changed, what I checked, and whether I disclosed it. Add three example rows for [my type of work] and a one-line disclosure sentence I can reuse.
